sources.title: Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, MIT lecture notes
locators: Sections 6.1–6.3: real, complex, and quaternionic matrix groups
Section 21.3 and Sections 23.3–23.6: exceptional root counts
Sections 31.2–31.3, Examples 31.3 and 31.10: spin groups and small-rank maps
Section 41.1, Exercise 41.3(iii), and Section 41.2: compact and split classical forms
Sections 43.1–43.3: compact and complex global forms; split real groups need not be simply connected

sources.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, second edition
locators: Propositions 1.136 and 1.139: compact SU and Sp; quaternionic-to-complex realization
Proposition 1.145: connectedness and the two components of SO(p,q) for p,q>0
sources.access: Read the author-hosted PDF in this review. Knapp indexes Sp by rank; catalogue uses complex/real matrix size.

mathematical_checks.claim: Distinct classical simple types begin at A1, B2, C3, D4.
mathematical_checks.reason: B1=C1=A1, B2=C2 and D3=A3 are duplicates; D2 is semisimple with two A1 factors.

mathematical_checks.claim: The classical cell dimensions are r(r+2), r(2r+1), r(2r+1), r(2r-1).
mathematical_checks.reason: Independent tangent-space count: trace zero removes one scalar from (r+1)^2; skew matrices in size 2r+1 or 2r have N(N-1)/2 parameters; symplectic block matrices have r^2+2r(r+1)/2 parameters. Substitution into the owner dimensions agrees.

mathematical_checks.claim: Exceptional dimensions are 14, 52, 78, 133 and 248 in G2,F4,E6,E7,E8 order.
Complex cells report complex dimension; underlying real dimension is twice as large.
mathematical_checks.reason: Each complex tangent coordinate contributes two real coordinates. Ambient complex or quaternionic matrices do not by themselves make U, SU, Sp, U(p,q), SU(p,q), Sp(p,q), or SL(n,H) complex Lie groups.

mathematical_checks.claim: Compact and complex cells select simply connected groups in the stated rank ranges. Split cells select SL and Sp matrix groups, SO0 matrix groups, or connected adjoint exceptional groups.
mathematical_checks.reason: The table does not promote algebraic simple connectivity to topological simple connectivity and does not describe every split representative as adjoint.

mathematical_checks.claim: SO0(p,q) is the identity component of full SO(p,q), with p negative and q positive directions.
mathematical_checks.reason: The new definition states p,q>=0 and p+q>=1. Its tangent-space count is correct. Compactness at pq=0 follows from SO(p+q); an explicit unbounded boost path proves noncompactness when pq>0. Its same-signature inclusion is an embedding, not an isomorphism for pq>0.

mathematical_checks.claim: The broad catalogue summaries retain full groups, scalar quotients, semidirect products, direct products, and Clifford coverings as distinct constructions.
mathematical_checks.reason: Read all 180 metadata records. Quaternionic and pseudo-unitary fields, symplectic pair-vs-matrix-size parameters, Spin(1)/Spin(2) boundary cases, and n=1 trivial groups do not receive false universal simply-connected or noncompact labels.

mathematical_checks.claim: Selected low-rank isomorphisms retain their proper global forms and relation kinds.
mathematical_checks.reason: Inspected the Spin(3/4/5/6) compact/complex isomorphisms, SU(2)->SO(3) covering, SL(2,C)->SO0(1,3) covering and PSL(2,C) real Lorentz isomorphism. Lie-algebra coincidences are not substituted for group isomorphisms.

resolved_findings.finding: The exactly-one statement previously included both B2 and C2.
resolved_findings.resolution: Root changed C to rank >=3 and explained the B2=C2 duplication.

resolved_findings.finding: The owner incorrectly claimed compact Sp(n) and split Sp(2n,R) have different real dimensions, and mixed the rank-indexed complex Sp notation with the catalogue convention.
resolved_findings.resolution: Both dimensions are now n(2n+1); complex realization now uses Sp(2n,C) and explicitly identifies the matrix-size convention.

resolved_findings.finding: Unqualified noncompactness incorrectly included the n=1 trivial group.
resolved_findings.resolution: Noncompactness and failure of simple connectivity are restricted to n>=2; n=1 is explicitly trivial, compact, simply connected.

resolved_findings.finding: Five compact exceptional construction summaries described the compact Lie algebra instead of its group.
resolved_findings.resolution: Each now explicitly describes the simply connected group integrating that compact real form.

resolved_findings.finding: The new symbolic-parameter SO0(p,q) record used status=defined.
resolved_findings.resolution: Changed status to family, consistent with its symbolic p,q parameters and the catalogue family distinction. Mathematical metadata, cells and source pages are unchanged.
resolved_findings.independent_verification: Reversing exactly this one status string reproduces the previous whole-file SHA-256 f3f8ecb211127f99e0600bb5a8f09c2770131f9564c84a007f8f11ba6abaa27a. All 180 metadata hashes, all 27 cell hashes and all 27 source-page hashes are unchanged; only the new SO0 object hash changes.

unknowns_and_exclusions.treatment: Absent compactness stays absent; it is not interpreted as false. Parameter-dependent properties remain strings with their original conditions. No attempt was made to fill every missing property.
